claims.text: Log-triglyceride values demonstrate within-person correlation coefficients of 0.64 over 4 years and 0.63 over 12 years.
The long-term stability of log-triglyceride values is similar to that of blood pressure and total serum cholesterol.
Adjustment for baseline values of established risk factors substantially attenuates the association between triglyceride values and coronary heart disease risk.
In the Reykjavik study, the adjusted odds ratio for coronary heart disease comparing the top third with the bottom third of usual log-triglyceride values is 1.76 (95% CI, 1.39 to 2.21).
In the EPIC-Norfolk study, the adjusted odds ratio for coronary heart disease comparing the top third with the bottom third of usual log-triglyceride values is 1.57 (95% CI, 1.10 to 2.24).

A meta-analysis of 29 studies shows an adjusted odds ratio for coronary heart disease of 1.72 (95% CI, 1.56 to 1.90) comparing individuals in the top third with those in the bottom third of usual log-triglyceride values.

methodologies.name: Nested case-control study and updated meta-analysis
methodologies.description: Evaluated serum triglyceride concentrations in two population-based cohort studies using nested case-control comparisons and combined results with a meta-analysis of 27 prospective studies.
conditions: Comparison of top third vs bottom third of log-triglyceride values
Adjustment for baseline values of established risk factors

limitations.text: The association between triglyceride concentrations and coronary heart disease risk depends considerably on levels of established risk factors, leaving the nature of any independent association unconfirmed.
Prior epidemiological studies had reported associations between serum triglyceride concentrations and coronary heart disease risk, but had not reliably quantified the association.

future_work.text: Further studies are needed to help assess the nature of any independent associations between triglyceride values and coronary heart disease risk.
